newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Overcrowded HK rejects 150 flight requests weekly.
newsitem.headline: Overcrowded HK rejects 150 flight requests weekly.

text.p: Hong Kong's Civil Aviation Department said it is turning down applications from airlines seeking an average of 150 extra flights a week in and out of the territory's Kai Tak airport.
Industry sources said airlines are constantly complaining of lack of slots at what is one of Asia's busiest international hubs but which is heavily constrained and exceeds design capacity.
The department told Reuters said it was unable to give an exact figure but the average of around 600 applications has been constant so far this year.
They were also unable provide a breakdown for applications from passenger and cargo airlines.

The Airport Authority Hong Kong, the body set up to oversee construction of the territory's new US$21 billion airport project, says Chek Lap Kok's twin runways are designed to solve Hong Kong's capacity crisis but the airport is not due to open until April 1998.
The figures show how much potential trade Hong Kong is losing and comes as Macau International Airport says it has attracted a fourth cargo airline - the second within a month.
Gemini Air Cargo flew the first of its four weekly flights from New York and Chicago into the Portuguese enclave about 50 miles across the Pearl River Delta from Hong Kong on September 27.
